# REST API: Credentials

---

The Credentials API helps you manage Public Keys or Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials in your Twilio account.

- Use public key credentials for [Public Key Client Validation](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/pkcv).
- Use AWS credentials to store Twilio Voice and Video recordings in AWS S3. Learn more about [storing Video recordings in AWS S3](https://twilio.com/docs/video/tutorials/storing-aws-s3) and [storing Voice recordings in AWS S3 (blog)](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/announcing-external-aws-s3-storage-support-for-voice-recordings).

---

## API Base URL

All URLs in the Credentials API reference documentation use the following base URL:

```
1https://accounts.twilio.com/v1/Credentials
2
```

The API is served over HTTPS. To ensure data privacy, unencrypted HTTP isn't supported.

---

## Authentication

To authenticate requests to the Twilio APIs, Twilio supports [HTTP Basic authentication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication). Use your *API key SID* as the username and your *API key secret* as the password. You can create an API key [in the Twilio Console](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/api-keys/keys-in-console) or [using the API](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/api-keys/key-resource-v1).

Learn more about [Twilio API authentication](https://twilio.com/docs/usage/requests-to-twilio).

List public keys

```
1curl -X GET "https://accounts.twilio.com/v1/Credentials/PublicKeys?PageSize=20" \
2-u $TWILIO_API_KEY:$TWILIO_API_SECRET
```

---

## Twilio SDKs

To interact with the `Credentials` endpoints, consider using the [Twilio SDKs](https://twilio.com/docs/libraries).

---

## Resources

The Credentials API contains the following resources:

| Resource | Description |
|---|---|
| [PublicKeys](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/credentialpublickey-resource) | Manage user-provided public keys. |
| [AWS](https://twilio.com/docs/iam/credentialaws-resource) | Manage user-provided AWS credentials. |
